description:
Advances: ancora.derive, ancora.findings

Ready-for: investigate

Symptom:
On a real feature branch, mix spec.check reported 39 errors, of which zero describe a contract that actually changed. Builder PR #165 (ChapterSpot/builder, branch feat/builder-xkg-atlas-obo, head 75cbd1fc, Ancora 1.0.0 pinned in mix.lock), CI run 34168086465, verdict line: "checked subjects=50 requirements=578 errors=39 warnings=0 ... spec.check result=fail tier=branch". Breakdown from the log:
- 32 errors are derived/drift (13 subjects x up to 2 functions) plus derived/growth on 13 subjects: builder.usage, builder.solutions, builder.workspaces_sensor, builder.llm_transport, builder.llm_instrumentation, builder.csm_agent, builder.config_editing, builder.agent.tool_error, builder.agent_models, builder.admin_panel, builder.feedback, builder.admin_capabilities, builder.skills. Every one is triggered by the same three bindings: Builder.Sessions.put_active_deploy/4 becoming /5 (a new subject_ref argument), Builder.Sessions.clear_active_deploy/1, and Builder.Agent.CSMAgent.Session.retry_last_async/1. The one subject whose contract those changes belong to, builder.deploy_shepherding, had its spec edited in the same diff and is clean. The other 13 are reached only because the large test files (test/builder/agent/csm_agent_test.exs, test/builder/agent/csm_agent/session_test.exs) carry @tag spec: for many subjects, and their shared setup calls those functions transitively.
- 7 errors are change/uncovered_file on lib/builder/auth.ex, lib/builder/auth/identity.ex, lib/builder_web.ex, lib/builder_web/endpoint.ex, lib/builder_web/router.ex, mix.exs, priv/repo/migrations/20260907195420_add_delegated_identities.exs. Five of those are infrastructure no unit test calls by design. The two auth modules are exercised through the Phoenix pipeline in ConnCase tests, which is exactly the limitation the repo already acknowledges with an overrides entry for builder.auth / derived/unanchored_subject; change/uncovered_file carries no subject ("-" in the log), so no overrides entry can reach it.

Why this is frustrating, stated plainly:
1. The prescribed remedy for drift ("edit the spec for this subject in the same diff") means writing fake requirement edits into 13 spec files whose behavior did not change. An honest implementer refuses, and the gate stays red. The alternative, a Spec-Ack trailer, is documented as "only for a mass mechanical edit whose diff does not change the contract", so using it here means bending the rule the tool wrote.
2. This is the third time the same repo hit the same shape. The builder-9q6 epic recorded it in August 2026 as a ticket-authoring lesson ("multi-mapped files engine.ex, session.ex compel co-changes on subject specs the Allowed list does not name"). Builder PR #164 on 2026-09-07 hit derived/drift on builder.chat_composer_formatting for Sessions.persist_message/3 the same way. Each time an agent spends a review round discovering that the finding is about attribution, not behavior.
3. Every touch of lib/builder/sessions.ex or lib/builder/agent/csm_agent/session.ex will reproduce this, because those modules sit under most subjects footprints. The gate is effectively red-by-default for the two most central files in the app.
4. Infra files (mix.exs, migrations, endpoint, router) can never be covered by a tagged test, so change/uncovered_file is a guaranteed error on any PR that adds a dep or a migration, and the only knob (lib_paths) is too coarse to exclude them without excluding real code.

Evidence:
- CI log: gh run view 34168086465 --repo ChapterSpot/builder --log, job "Checks / Spec Check". Grep for "[ERROR]" and "spec.check result=".
- Categorized extract saved during triage at /tmp/spec165.txt on the monitoring machine (42 lines; 7 uncovered_file, 32 drift+growth across 13 subjects).
- Builder config: .spec/config.yml in ChapterSpot/builder (severities: derived/growth error, change/uncovered_file error; six overrides all for derived/unanchored_subject; no path-level exclusions possible because config only accepts default_base, test_paths, lib_paths, severities, overrides).
- Prior occurrence: bw show builder-9q6 comments dated 2026-08-09 ("TICKET-AUTHORING DEFECTS", item 1) in ChapterSpot/builder.
- Where attribution happens in this repo: lib/ancora/derive/membership.ex and lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex (footprints follow calls from tagged tests, no notion of a shared helper or a multi-subject test file); lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex:28-38 (uncovered_file is any changed path under lib_paths not in the covered set; no subject, no per-path override).

Why now:
1.2.0 (2026-09-05) added the surface: spec-meta key so drift on non-surface files becomes derived/drift_transitive at info. That addresses part of finding 1 but only when every subject opts in with a surface list, it does nothing for derived/growth on the same subjects, and Builder is still on 1.0.0. Nothing in 1.2.0 touches change/uncovered_file scoping. The Builder OBO work (three PRs, one blocked on this) is the first launch-critical branch to be held by the gate rather than by code, and Manuel has authorized a Spec-Ack trailer on that PR as a temporary bypass, which is exactly the escape hatch the docs say not to use for this.

Suspected cause:
Hypothesis: footprint attribution treats every call reachable from a test tagged to subject S as part of S contract, with no distinction between the function under test and shared setup or fixtures. A per-subject surface list moves the burden onto every spec author; a better default may be to attribute a call to a subject only when it is made from the test body (not setup/describe-level helpers or test/support), or to weight a multi-subject file by which subject tag is nearest the call. Separately, change/uncovered_file needs either a subject so overrides can reach it, or a config list of paths that are declared uncovered by design (migrations, mix.exs, endpoint/router).
title: spec.check fans drift/growth across unrelated subjects and flags untestable infra files, with no way to scope either
